hounds.name: The Desk
hounds.tagline: Four analysts, a bull, a bear and a desk head argue every game in the open.
hounds.style: AI desk: analysts, bull and bear, desk head
hounds.rule_text: Four AI analysts (stats, situation and news, market, injuries and lineups) each write a checked report from the same frozen data. A bull and a bear then argue from those reports, and a desk head reads everything and may take at most two bets at the best quoted price, or pass the whole game. Code strikes any bet at -200 or worse, any price not in the data, and any bet whose stated probability does not beat both the books' own de-vigged number and the break-even of the average price. Every claim is checked against the data. One model reading, unproven; paper only.

hounds.name: The Sharp
hounds.tagline: Only bets when the best price beats the books' own number.
hounds.rule_text: An AI persona that ignores narratives. It takes a selection only when the break-even probability of the best quoted price is below the books' de-vigged fair probability, with a stated probability that beats the market's number and the average price, at most two bets a game. Code strikes any bet at -200 or worse or at a price not in the data. One model reading, unproven; paper only.

hounds.name: The Square
hounds.tagline: Favourites and overs. The control for what a casual bettor takes.
hounds.rule_text: A deliberate control. An AI persona that takes only the moneyline favourite or the Over on the game total, never an underdog, an under, a spread, a team total or a prop, with a stated probability that beats the market's number and the average price, at most two bets a game. Code strikes any bet at -200 or worse. One model reading, unproven; paper only.

hounds.name: The Fader
hounds.tagline: Takes the other side of what the favourite and the over suggest.
hounds.rule_text: An AI persona that fades the popular side, using the favourite and the over as its stand-in because the data holds no betting percentages. It takes only a moneyline underdog, a side that gets points, or an Under, with a stated probability that beats the market's number and the average price, at most two bets a game. Code strikes any bet at -200 or worse. One model reading, unproven; paper only.

hounds.name: The Weather Nerd
hounds.tagline: Totals only: weather, park, and the conditions of the game.
hounds.rule_text: An AI persona that bets the game total and team totals only, reading weather, park and the scoring conditions in the data. It says so when the data holds no weather. Stated probability must beat the market's number and the average price, at most two bets a game. Code strikes any bet at -200 or worse. One model reading, unproven; paper only.

hounds.name: The Grinder
hounds.tagline: Unders and short favourites, never a big claim.
hounds.rule_text: An AI persona that takes only an Under, or a moneyline favourite priced -150 or shorter. Its stated probability must beat the market's number and the average price but may exceed the books' fair probability by at most 5 percentage points; a larger claimed gap is struck by code. At most two bets a game; any bet at -200 or worse is struck. One model reading, unproven; paper only.

hounds.name: The Historian
hounds.tagline: Head-to-head and series history, nothing else.
hounds.rule_text: An AI persona that argues only from head-to-head and series history. Every reason behind a bet must cite that history (or a price or the game block), and at least one must cite the history; code strikes any bet that does not. Stated probability must beat the market's number and the average price, at most two bets a game; any bet at -200 or worse is struck. One model reading, unproven; paper only.
